haiku-low.q1: The indexer deletes the product's search document, because only active rows appear in search; the change carries its commit_lsn version.
haiku-low.q2: The older change is a version conflict, so it is stale: counted in stale_total, not applied, and not an error. The newer version stays.
haiku-low.q3: It retries only the failed documents, in the same order with the same versions, backing off 1 s, 2 s, 4 s up to 60 s. The partition stays paused and never skips ahead.
haiku-low.q4: The indexer produces the original event and error to catalog.products.dlq, waits for the ack, alerts search on-call, and carries on. Later valid changes still apply.
haiku-low.q5: Ops drop the slot at 50 GB, the connector fails, and only a full rebuild recovers. Updates in the gap are lost; recreate the slot and restart the connector first.
haiku-low.q6: The alias products moves in one atomic request, after the gate holds 3 checks in a row: lag under 5 s, count within 0.5%, no unreviewed DLQ events. A person approves the first switch.
haiku-low.q7: In the consumer group's committed offsets. They advance after each batch, up to the last resolved event per partition, once every document is written, stale, or confirmed in the DLQ.
haiku-low.q8: It resumes from the committed offsets. Replayed events are harmless: equal versions are accepted and older ones conflict, so the end state is correct.
haiku-low.q9: Saved start offsets are read before the snapshot opens, so later changes sit at or after them. After the load, the new group replays from those offsets in order, last event wins.
haiku-low.q10: Version 0, so any replayed event can overwrite a snapshot row.
haiku-low.q11: The old index keeps its own consumer group and stays in sync for 48 h. Rollback is an atomic alias swap back once the old group is under 5 s behind. After 48 h without rollback, the old index and its group are deleted.
haiku-low.q12: The live index is untouched and keeps serving. A failed copy cannot resume: alert, then the operator restarts under a new name. A failed catch-up keeps catching up, with an alert after 6 h if the gate is unmet.

sonnet.q1: The document is deleted from the index (create/update with a status other than active maps to a delete, written with commit_lsn as version).
sonnet.q2: The older change carries a lower commit_lsn version, so the store returns a version conflict. The indexer treats it as stale, counts it in stale_total, does not treat it as an error, and moves on. The newer data stays.
sonnet.q3: It retries only the failed docs, in the same order and with the same versions. It backs off 1 s, 2 s, 4 s and so on, capped at 60 s. The partition stays paused and it never skips ahead. Offsets are not committed past them. It alerts if stuck at the 60 s cap for more than 5 minutes.
sonnet.q4: The original event and the error are produced to catalog.products.dlq, and the indexer waits for the ack. The search on-call is alerted and the indexer carries on and commits offsets. A later valid change to the same product is still applied. A person can replay the DLQ event by hand after the cause is fixed. If the DLQ produce fails, it is treated as a transient failure: backoff, partition paused, offsets not committed.
sonnet.q5: Ops drop the slot and the connector fails (slot missing). Updates between the drop and the new slot are lost. Recovery is a full rebuild: recreate search_slot, restart the connector, then run the rebuild into a new index and switch the alias. The old index is not a clean rollback target for the gap.
sonnet.q6: The alias products is moved from the old index to the new one in one atomic request (remove products_v3, add products_vN), so a query goes to one or the other, never neither. Before that, the gate must hold on 3 checks in a row, checked every minute. Lag must be under 5 s. The doc count must be within 0.5% of the active row count. There must be no unreviewed DLQ events from this group since its start offsets. A person approves the first switch.
sonnet.q7: In the consumer group's committed Kafka offsets (for example indexer-products_v3). They are advanced only after every document up to them is acknowledged: written, stale (conflict), or confirmed in the DLQ.
sonnet.q8: It resumes from the last committed offsets and replays the events. Replays are harmless: an equal version is accepted and older versions conflict. A replay may briefly bring a document back and then delete it again, but the end state is correct.
sonnet.q9: The controller records the end offsets of all 12 partitions before opening the snapshot, and saves them as the start offsets. After the load finishes, the new group indexer-products_vN starts at those offsets and replays the topic. Events committed before the snapshot are harmless because replay applies them again in order and the last event wins. Replay starts only after the load finishes.
sonnet.q10: Version 0, so any replayed event can overwrite them.
sonnet.q11: The old index keeps its own consumer group and stays in sync with the topic for 48 h. Rollback is an atomic alias swap back, after confirming the old group's lag is under 5 s, so no change is lost. After 48 h with no rollback, the old index is deleted and its consumer group is stopped and deleted. If a rollback happens, the new index and its group are kept until a person deletes them.
sonnet.q12: Search is unaffected. The live index is not touched during the build and keeps serving through the alias, and the new index is invisible to search until the switch. If the loader crashes or the snapshot is lost, the snapshot cannot be resumed. The controller alerts the search on-call, and the operator deletes products_vN and restarts under a new name with new start offsets. If catch-up is slow, the gate is not met, the group keeps catching up, and it alerts after 6 h. The alias does not move.
